at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

at-0002.title: Convert amounts via to_money, never floats
at-0002.content: Convert raw amounts to Decimal with ledgerly.money.to_money before arithmetic; it rejects float and bool inputs with a BillingError, so never pass floats into money math.

last_failure.review_comment: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0003.title: Raise BillingError with machine-readable codes
at-0003.content: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly/errors.py` with short machine-readable codes such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`; do not raise bare ValueError.

at-0004.title: Exclude bool when validating integer inputs
at-0004.content: When validating an integer parameter, check `isinstance(x, bool)` first because `bool` is a subclass of `int`; otherwise `True`/`False` slip through as 1/0.
